axes.xDefinition: log10 stellar mass within a 3D aperture of 50 kpc (a lognormal mass error, 0.07 dex at z = 0, is added to every simulated mass before counting)
axes.yDefinition: log10 number density per dex of stellar mass (the axis reads Mpc^-3; the boxes are given in comoving Mpc)

selection.population: galaxies of the calibration volume (VELOCIraptor subhaloes)
selection.warning: Galaxy stellar mass function at z = 0 of the FLAMINGO m8 calibration simulation run with the best-fitting subgrid parameters in a (100 Mpc)^3 volume (1.34e+08 Msun baryonic particles), read from the red path of Fig. 8 of Kugel et al. 2023 and cut at the 10-particle limit (M* = 9.13; fainter bins are drawn dotted and grey). The simulated masses are 3D 50 kpc aperture masses to which a random lognormal error of 0.07 dex (z = 0) is added, as the paper does to mimic observational errors (an Eddington-like bias), so the high-mass end is steeper-looking than the plain aperture masses give. The model was fitted to this curve between log M* = 8.67 and 11.5, so it is not a prediction there. The paper does not say whether satellites and subhaloes without stars enter the count. The box is small, so the highest-mass bins hold few galaxies. The paper says the Chabrier (2003) IMF is used for the stars.

axes.xDefinition: log10 M500c (mass inside R500c, the radius enclosing 500 times the critical density)

selection.population: haloes of the calibration volume (bins hold at least ten haloes)
selection.warning: Median gas fraction inside R500c at z = 0.1 against M500c of the FLAMINGO m8 calibration simulation run with the best-fitting subgrid parameters in a (100 Mpc)^3 volume, read from the red path of Fig. 8 of Kugel et al. 2023 (adaptive bins of at least ten haloes between 1e13 and 1e15 Msun; the statistic is not stated: the paper takes the median and the 16th-84th percentiles of each bin for the fit) and divided by Omega_b/Omega_m = 0.0486/0.306. The model was fitted to X-ray gas fractions at z = 0.1 up to M500c = 10^13.73 Msun and to weak lensing at z = 0.3, so this curve is a calibration target, not a prediction, and the observations it was fitted to carry a hydrostatic mass bias that the paper fits (b = 0.743). The small box holds few clusters, so the highest bins are noisy.
